subject: HealthSync — post-call technical synthesis & next steps
body:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthsync.co>, Elena Ruiz <elena@healthsync.co>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: HealthSync — post-call technical synthesis & next steps

Hi Liam / Elena,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the detailed walkthrough of HealthSync's user flows. Below is a concise synthesis of what we heard, plus technical clarifications and proposed next steps. I want to make sure we capture the constraints that matter for final topology and SOW pricing.

Summary (pain points & goals)
- Latency is user-facing: search completions and note summarization must feel sub-300ms for the majority of requests; 95th pct target is 350ms, but you care about P99 spikes during peaks.
- Throughput: baseline ~120 reqs/s during business hours, with peak bursts up to ~650 reqs/s for short windows (30–45 min).
- Model quality: prefer an open model family that supports coherent medical summarization and redaction-friendly outputs. You want a reproducible model variant that avoids hallucinations in clinical contexts.
- Data residency & security: all PHI remains in your VPC; Redwood Private or Dedicated with customer-controlled KMS is required for the pilot.
- Cost / operational controls: need clear levers (batching, quantization, KV caching) to keep per-call cost predictable.

Call technical notes (items Karthik can speak to)
- SLOs we discussed: target P95 <= 350ms, target P99 <= 800ms, availability SLA 99.9% for pilot.
- Workload characteristics: median prompt length ~420 tokens, median completion ~60 tokens. Prefix reuse is high for summarization flow (approx 60% reuse within a session).
- Model plan: recommend starting with an FP16 8-bit quantized variant of an open decoder model (we discussed the tradeoffs). For latency-sensitive hits, we propose a trimmed-context config and a higher-throughput variant for batch scoring.
- Topology options: (1) Redwood Private in your VPC using dedicated GPU pool (preferred for security + predictable latency), (2) Hybrid — hosted control plane + local inference nodes for PHI workloads, (3) Hosted Dedicated in our DCs with dedicated capacity and VPC peering if you prefer managed infra.

Open technical questions we need from you
- Can you confirm 95th/99th percentile latency tolerance for the pilot workload (we have your numbers above but want written confirmation)?
- Example traffic shape: can you attach a 48-hour and 7-day traces csv (timestamp, qps, avg tokens) so we can run a capacity simulation?
- Any hard limits on ephemeral storage for KV cache or GPU memory allocation per instance?

Attachments shared
- healthsync_prod_requirements.xlsx (you uploaded during call) — saved to the folder linked below.
- proposed_topology_sketch.png (sketch we annotated during the call).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — draft timeline
1) By Apr 8: HealthSync sends traffic traces + compliance checklist response.
2) Apr 9–12: Redwood runs capacity simulation and returns two recommended topologies (costed) + SLO projection.
3) Apr 15: Joint call to review topology & finalize pilot SLOs.
4) Apr 20–30: Pilot deployment (1-week soak) in Dedicated/Private config.

Next steps (concrete asks)
- Liam/Elena: please send the 48h/7-day traces and confirm P95/P99 targets.
- I'll share a short tech appendix and an initial cost sketch (will include the throughput vs. quantization sensitivity table).

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192
https://redwood.ai

----

> - P95/P99 targets: confirm P95 <= 350ms, P99 <= 800ms for the pilot (we'll sign off on those).
> - Traffic traces: attaching a 48-hour export (see the sheet "qps_48h.csv" in the xlsx). Peak pattern is usually 09:45–10:30 and 15:00–15:40 PDT.

On Sun, 04 Apr 2027 02:18:12 +0000, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:

> From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
> To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthsync.co>, Elena Ruiz <elena@healthsync.co>
> Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
> Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 02:18:12 +0000
> Subject: Re: HealthSync — post-call technical synthesis & next steps>
>
> Hi Liam / Elena — thanks for the quick confirmations and for the trace export. A few technical notes from my side after a quick pass: 
>
> 1) Capacity simulation assumptions I used (we'll run a more exhaustive scan once we have the raw tokens distribution):
>    - baseline qps: 120 req/s; peak burst qps: 650 req/s for ~40 minutes; median prompt tokens: 420; median completion tokens: 60.
>    - KV cache hit assumed 60% for summarization sessions; this saves ~40% of per-token GPU work for those flows.
>
> 2) Preliminary topology recommendation (pilot):
>    - 8 x A5000-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool (Private deployment), each node running 2 inference workers with continuous batching tuned for 12–20ms batching delay to preserve latency.
>    - KV shard per node, prefix cache using local NVMe to minimize cold-starts.
>    - Fallback path: lighter quantized model (Q5_K_M or similar) for low-cost degradation under extreme bursts; route policy by latency tier.
>
> 3) Latency projections (ballpark from quick sim):
>    - P50 ~ 120–160ms; P95 ~ 300–360ms (depends on batching latency tuning); P99 ~ 750–920ms during peak burst if fallback not engaged.
>
> 4) Data residency + KMS: Private deployment + your KMS is the straightest path. We'll include HSM/KMS integration steps in the SOW draft.
>
> 5) Items we need to size accurately: max concurrency per session, average number of sessions per user, and any long-running streaming completions.
>
> I'll turn this into a short appendix with two alternative capacity/cost scenarios (conservative + optimized) and share by Apr 9.
>
> Karthik
> Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
>
